title: Roster model
description: One concrete model, bound to the harness that can run it. The only place a wire model identifier appears.

id.description: Friendly id used by playbooks, e.g. fable-5-1.

profile.description: Configuration profile on that adapter. DeepSeek-via-Claude (`deepseek`) is a profile of the claude adapter, not a separate adapter.

model.description: The identifier the harness itself expects, e.g. claude-fable-5-1.

efforts.description: Effort levels this model supports on this harness. [] means the model supports NO effort setting — a real, verified fact. null means UNKNOWN — nobody has established it. Both reject a playbook naming an effort, but for different reasons and with different fixes.

defaultEffort.description: null when the model takes no effort setting (efforts: []). Otherwise must appear in efforts.

credentialRef.description: A reference only — env:NAME, file:/path, keyring:NAME. Never a credential value. The loader rejects anything that does not match this shape.

account.description: Another PERSON's login on the same provider, not another provider. Several people collaborating through one panel each have their own subscription; an account names an isolated config directory that person logs into once, and changes nothing else about the connection. Mutually exclusive with endpointRef/credentialRef, which describe a different provider rather than a different login.

endpointRef.description: Reference to a base URL override, for provider profiles such as DeepSeek.

verification.description: Whether this entry's claims have been established. An unverified model loads for preview but cannot be used in a live run.

method.description: How it was established, e.g. 'codex --help + a probe turn'.

then.description: defaultEffort must appear in efforts; enforced by the loader, which JSON Schema cannot express across siblings.

then.$comment: An account is another person's login on the SAME provider. endpointRef/credentialRef describe a different provider, and a non-default profile is provider routing — either would label the connection as something it is not.
